function.description: Continue pending messages omitted by memcal_open, using its cursor. Messages are nominated for this entry, not every message in the thread. Reading does not review them; cite line ids in a correction or memcal_reviewed.
function.name: memcal_activity

cursor.description: an archive id to read after (for paging)

function.description: Add one private memory event. Use memcal_schedule for recurring events, including several weekdays; do not add each weekday separately. Tentative plans are allowed. Use memcal_update for an existing event.
function.name: memcal_add

context_source_ids.description: background archive ids; no field authority. Only valid with field_sources.

field_sources.description: map of field name → archive line ids supporting that field (newest timestamp wins per field). Prefer over flat source_ids when fields have different supporting messages.

kind.description: commitment = they are doing it; availability = someone else's state ('Alex free Monday'); opportunity = something they could go to but have not committed to

location.description: Place, address, or video-call URL; omit if unknown

note.description: Other event details in plain text

participants.description: full names where known, not the user

series.description: the recurring thing this is one of, as a slug ('tutoring'). Sets it where repetition alone could not prove it — a new instance then starts with what the series already knows

source_ids.description: archive line ids supporting this creation (flat). Do not combine with field_sources.

status.description: declined = not going. confirmed = locked in. happened = done.

subject.description: whose thing this is; 'me' unless it is someone else's state or plan

title.description: short, as a person would say it

until.description: last day, for things spanning days

function.description: Two names, one person: a legal name behind a nickname, a surname arriving late. Points the other name at the page that already exists so it never gets a second one. Only on evidence the user gave you — merging two real people is not recoverable, and two friends sharing a first name is the opposite situation.
function.name: memcal_alias

page.description: the page that already exists, e.g. 'robbie'

function.description: Resolve anything the brief is holding open — an 'Ask about' question OR an 'Open' to-do — when the user tells you the answer or says it's done. This is how those loops close; nothing closes by inference.
function.name: memcal_answer

question.description: distinctive words from the question or to-do

function.description:
Read a stretch of the conversation a memory came out of, in order, as it was actually said. Use after memcal_open_source when the cited lines are not enough — the user asks 'what were they talking about', 'who else was in on it', 'what did they decide' — or to check a row against what was really said.
Give it the id of a line (every line from memcal_open_source, memcal_conversation and memcal_search_archive carries one) and it returns the messages around that moment. Or give a channel and thread for the tail of a conversation.
function.name: memcal_conversation

channel.description: imessage | groupme | whatsapp | email | ical | agent

line_id.description: id of a line to centre on, from any memcal result

function.description: Delete a row that should never have been there — a newsletter that became an event, something about a person the user does not know. NOT for things they are simply not attending: that is memcal_update with status 'declined', which keeps the row so it stops being suggested.
function.name: memcal_drop

which.description: the row's E# handle or distinctive words

function.description: List a day or date range beyond the brief, using plain date words or YYYY-MM-DD and days. For a year, use YYYY-01-01 with days=365 (366 in a leap year). Weekly overviews within the brief need no lookup.
function.name: memcal_list_days

days.description: how many days from there; default 1

function.description: List a whole calendar month, YYYY-MM. For one day or a short range use memcal_list_days. Weekly overviews within the brief need no lookup.
function.name: memcal_list_month

function.description: Two rows are the same thing — 'the Rowan meetup IS the beer garden'. Folds one into the other: details pool, guest lists combine, the duplicate goes away. Only when the user says they are one event; two similar plans on nearby days are usually two plans.
function.name: memcal_merge

drop.description: the duplicate row's E# handle or distinctive words

keep.description: the surviving row's E# handle or distinctive words — prefer the more specific one

function.description: Move or cancel one occurrence without changing the series. Use an event E# handle, or the series name plus on for a date not yet materialized. Give to for a move; cancelled=true skips it without requiring to.
function.name: memcal_move_once

cancelled.description: the week is skipped, not moved

on.description: Original occurrence date when which names the series

which.description: the row's E# handle when available, otherwise distinctive words

function.description:
Remember or correct one fact. page='me' stores a fact about the user; updating the same fact replaces its value while retaining history. Record a durable fact about a person, place, or project on their wiki page — a role, a relationship, an interest, where they live. Use this when the user states something that will still be true next month, so it lands as a labelled fact instead of a sentence the nightly pass has to re-derive.
One fact per call: page='quinn delgado', slot='likes', value='Pokemon'. The slot is the label; the value is the bare answer, not a sentence. Only what the user actually said — if you are inferring it, ask instead.
function.name: memcal_note

page.description: who or what this is about, e.g. 'Quinn Brooks'; 'me' for the user

section.description: omit unless it is obviously not a person

slot.description: the label, e.g. 'likes', 'dungeon master for', 'works at'

function.description: Open a brief handle or wiki page for details and history. Includes labeled citations, nearby context, and capped pending messages. Use memcal_activity only to continue omitted messages. Accepts E#, T#, Q#, page names, aliases, or me.
function.name: memcal_open

ref.description: brief handle (E258), page name, alias, or me

function.description:
Read full original messages or email when memcal_open's details and linked evidence are not enough. Open the relevant record with memcal_open first; use this for a fuller quotation or verification against the source. Brief handles include E46, T3, Q5, or S1. Lines marked as evidence are what the row was built from; the rest is nearby conversation. If it comes back saying there is no line-level citation, say so — that row is a summary of a conversation, not a quote from it, and it may simply be wrong.
For the wider conversation around it, follow up with memcal_conversation.
function.name: memcal_open_source

function.description: Re-render the current brief on demand — the same snapshot prefetch injects, without model work. For turns where injection may have been skipped or source state changed mid-turn.
function.name: memcal_refresh

function.description: Mark activity lines as reviewed with no change to the row — the stored plan still stands after reading them. Only the cited lines stop raising hints. Cite the line ids memcal_open or memcal_activity returned.
function.name: memcal_reviewed

source_ids.description: archive line ids this review covered

function.description: Create or change ONE recurring series. weekdays lists all days: Monday/Wednesday/Friday is one weekly rule. interval repeats every N days/weeks/months. starting dates a change while preserving the earlier schedule. status paused/active/ended pauses, resumes, or stops it. Use memcal_move_once for one occurrence.
function.name: memcal_schedule

ended.description: only when they say they stopped

location.description: Place, address, or video-call URL; omit if unknown

starting.description: the day the new schedule begins; omit for 'from now on'. Never retro-dates what already happened

status.description: Pause, resume (active), or stop the series, from starting

weekday.description: 'tuesday', for a single weekly day; prefer weekdays

weekdays.description: All repeating days, e.g. [monday, wednesday, friday]; one series

which.description: the recurring thing, as a name or slug ('tutoring')

function.description: Search original messages when records and wiki facts do not answer. Filter by person, channel, or date; query may be empty with filters. Results include line_id for reading surrounding conversation.
function.name: memcal_search_archive

channel.description: imessage | groupme | whatsapp | email | ical | agent

person.description: who said it, or who it is with

query.description: words to look for; may be empty

function.description: Find remembered facts when the page is unknown. Searches names, aliases, fact labels, values, and prose. Use before searching original messages.
function.name: memcal_search_wiki

query.description: name, alias, fact label, value, or prose to find

function.description: Something the user said they would do. Short imperative, their words. Use wake_condition when it should wait on something ('Rowan is back from Italy') rather than on a date. Use event to link an obligation to an existing occasion; it then expires when that event is over. done=true closes one they say they have finished — any distinctive words from it will find it.
function.name: memcal_todo

done.description: close the to-do named by text instead of opening one

event.description: event E# handle, key, or distinctive words naming it

remind.description: Set when the user wants poking about this rather than just a record of it. 'yes' picks the hour — 09:00 the day before whatever it is anchored to — or give an ISO datetime to say exactly when. Needs a due date or an event to count back from. It reaches their phone and their Telegram, so only when the user asked to be reminded.

wake_condition.description: what has to become true before asking

function.description: Update one event by its E# handle or distinctive title. Omitted fields stay unchanged; an empty string clears an optional detail. Use status declined for cancellation or non-attendance. Use memcal_schedule to change a series. Returns the updated record; no verification read needed.
function.name: memcal_update

context_source_ids.description: background archive ids; no field authority. Only valid with field_sources.

field_sources.description: map of field name → archive line ids supporting that field (newest timestamp wins per field). Prefer over flat source_ids when fields have different supporting messages.

kind.description: commitment = they are doing it; availability = someone else's state ('Alex free Monday'); opportunity = something they could go to but have not committed to

location.description: Place, address, or video-call URL; omit if unknown

note.description: a detail with nowhere else to go

series.description: the recurring thing this is one of, as a slug ('tutoring'). Sets it where repetition alone could not prove it — a new instance then starts with what the series already knows

source_ids.description: archive line ids from memcal_open or memcal_activity (flat oldest-line). Do not combine with field_sources.

status.description: declined = not going. confirmed = locked in. happened = done.

subject.description: whose thing this is; only to correct a row filed under the wrong person

title.description: only to correct a wrong one

until.description: last day, for things spanning days

which.description: the row's E# handle when available, otherwise distinctive words
